I haven't shipped v2.3.2 or opened the incident. The deploy needs change-manager approval first, and I don't have it.

**Why it needs approval:** v2.3.2 has never run in production. It doesn't appear anywhere in checkout-api's release history: v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 were healthy, v2.3.1 is unhealthy, and v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging. Our policy says deploying a version that has never been healthy in production needs change-manager sign-off. Even a hotfix counts.

**Why I held the incident too:** you asked for a SEV3 recording the change. Since the change hasn't happened, opening one now would record something that didn't occur and page on-call for no reason.

**Current state:** all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are running v2.3.1. The service is unhealthy with an 18% error rate.

**Options:**
1. **Get approval:** once change-manager approves v2.3.2, tell me and I'll deploy it to all regions, then open the SEV3.
2. **Roll back now:** if you need the errors to stop sooner, I can roll back to v2.3.0. It was the last healthy version and doesn't need approval. Then v2.3.2 can follow once it's approved.
3. **Open an incident now:** I can open an incident for the current v2.3.1 errors. Given 18% errors in every region, it may deserve more than SEV3.

Which would you like?
